mcqs.question: Which of the following best illustrates that gases have no fixed shape?

options.A: A balloon that can be squeezed into any container
options.B: An ice cube that keeps its shape

mcqs.answer: A balloon that can be squeezed into any container
mcqs.explanation: A gas takes the shape of whatever container it is in, so a balloon that can be squeezed to fit any container shows that gases have no fixed shape. The other options describe solids or liquids, which retain shape.

mcqs.question: A gas is released into a large empty jar. Which statement is true about the gas?

options.A: It expands to fill the entire jar
options.B: It stays as a small puff in one corner
options.D: It keeps the same volume it had before being released

mcqs.answer: It expands to fill the entire jar
mcqs.explanation: Gases have no fixed volume; they spread out to occupy the whole volume of the container. Options B, C, and D contradict this property.

mcqs.question: A student thinks a gas will only occupy the bottom part of a container, leaving empty space above. Which statement correctly corrects this misconception?

options.A: The gas spreads out to fill the entire container, including the space above.
options.B: The gas stays at the bottom like a liquid.
options.C: The gas rises and stays only at the top of the container.
options.D: The gas occupies exactly half of the container’s volume.

mcqs.answer: The gas spreads out to fill the entire container, including the space above.
mcqs.explanation: Gases fill all the available space because their particles move freely in all directions. The other options describe behaviours of liquids or are arbitrary.

mcqs.question: Why can gases flow easily from one place to another?

options.A: Because their particles are far apart and move freely.
options.B: Because their particles are tightly packed together.
options.C: Because the particles are glued to each other.

mcqs.answer: Because their particles are far apart and move freely.
mcqs.explanation: The large distances between gas particles allow them to slide past each other, giving gases the ability to flow. Tight packing, glue‑like forces, or heaviness would hinder flow.

mcqs.question: Which statement correctly compares the compressibility of gases with that of liquids?

options.A: Gases are much more compressible than liquids.
options.B: Liquids are more compressible than gases.
options.C: Both gases and liquids are equally compressible.
options.D: Neither gases nor liquids can be compressed.

mcqs.answer: Gases are much more compressible than liquids.
mcqs.explanation: Because gas particles are far apart, they can be pushed closer together, making gases highly compressible. Liquids have particles much closer together, so they are only slightly compressible. Options B, C, and D are incorrect.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is NOT an example of a gas at room temperature?
mcqs.explanation: Oxygen, carbon dioxide, and water vapor are all gases under normal conditions. Granular sugar is a solid, not a gas. Hence option D is the correct answer.

mcqs.question: Which statement correctly describes a property of gases?

options.C: They are rigid like a solid.
options.D: They retain the shape of the container they were poured from.

mcqs.explanation: Gases take the shape of the container they occupy, meaning they have no fixed shape. Options B, C, and D contradict this fundamental property.

mcqs.question: What is true about the volume of a gas?

options.A: It takes the volume of its container.
options.B: It has a fixed volume regardless of the container.
options.C: It cannot change its volume under any condition.
options.D: It is always larger than the container’s volume.

mcqs.answer: It takes the volume of its container.
mcqs.explanation: A gas expands or contracts to fill the entire volume of the container it is in, showing it has no fixed volume. The other options misstate this behavior.
